subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: Which scoped inbound-media ownership model should OpenClaw support for multi-agent deployments before implementation: account, resolved agent, session/tenant, channel/chat provenance, or an explicit sharing contract?
rationale: The source-level problem is clear, but choosing the wrong scope can either leave cross-agent leakage in place or break existing managed-media references, channel behavior, and compatibility for flat inbound files.

options.title: Define one scoped media contract
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad design owner and implement storage, resolver, staging, cleanup, docs, and tests together.

options.title: Limit to account-scoped saves
options.body: Implement the narrower account-ID directory approach while explicitly leaving sessions, tenants, channel provenance, and sharing as follow-up work.

options.title: Defer core isolation
options.body: Document current flat inbound behavior and leave operators responsible for filesystem isolation, accepting the privacy gap for now.

recommendation.title: Define one scoped media contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad design owner and implement storage, resolver, staging, cleanup, docs, and tests together.

likelyOwner.reason: The core media store, managed-reference, and staging history most strongly routes through this owner trail.
